name: github-copilot-llm-gateway
description: Connect GitHub Copilot to self-hosted models on any OpenAI-compatible server, with fixes for tool calls, reasoning and context limits

apiKey.title: API Key
apiKey.description: Optional bearer token sent to the inference server. Leave blank for unauthenticated local servers (vLLM, Ollama, llama.cpp). Stored by VS Code; takes precedence over the 'Configure Server' command's SecretStorage entry.

github.copilot.llm-gateway.serverUrl.description: Inference server URL (OpenAI API compatible endpoint)

github.copilot.llm-gateway.apiKey.description: Deprecated. Use the 'Configure Server' command to store the API key in VS Code's secret storage. Any value entered here is migrated and cleared on extension activation.
github.copilot.llm-gateway.apiKey.deprecationMessage: API keys are now stored in VS Code's secret storage. Use the 'GitHub Copilot LLM Gateway: Configure Server' command to set the API key.

github.copilot.llm-gateway.defaultMaxTok.markdownDescription: Fallback context window size (total tokens) used **only** when the server does not report one in `/v1/models`. It never overrides a server-reported value — to force a specific size for a model, use `modelContextWindows` instead.

github.copilot.llm-gateway.defaultMaxOut.description: Fallback maximum output tokens when the server does not report max_output_tokens. Thinking models spend part of this budget on reasoning before answering, so keep it generous; it is always clamped to fit the model's context window.

github.copilot.llm-gateway.enableImageIn.description: Enable image input capability for models that support multimodal requests

github.copilot.llm-gateway.enableToolCal.description: Enable tool calling capability for models

github.copilot.llm-gateway.parallelToolC.description: Allow model to call multiple tools in parallel (disable if model has issues with parallel calls)

github.copilot.llm-gateway.agentTemperat.description: Fallback temperature for agent/tool calling mode (lower = more consistent tool call formatting). Set to 0.0 for best results with fine-tuned models. A temperature discovered from the backend's own model config (e.g. an Ollama Modelfile via /api/show) takes precedence; use perModelOptions to force a specific value.

github.copilot.llm-gateway.verboseLoggin.description: When enabled, the full chat request body (including messages and tool args) is written to the output channel, along with each inline completion request (model, prompt size, max_tokens, timeout) and its outcome. Keep disabled unless you are reproducing an issue — captured logs may contain conversation content from the user's current editor.

github.copilot.llm-gateway.customHeaders.description: Deprecated. Use the 'Edit Custom Headers' command to store headers in VS Code's secret storage. Any value entered here is migrated and cleared on extension activation.
github.copilot.llm-gateway.customHeaders.deprecationMessage: Custom headers (which may carry credentials such as 'Authorization') are now stored in VS Code's secret storage. Use the 'GitHub Copilot LLM Gateway: Edit Custom Headers' command.

github.copilot.llm-gateway.extraModelOpt.description: Extra parameters merged into the chat-completions request body (e.g. top_k, repetition_penalty, seed). Per-request modelOptions from the caller take precedence. Edit in settings.json for non-string values.

github.copilot.llm-gateway.perModelOptio.description: Per-model chat-completion parameters, keyed by model id. Merged on top of 'extraModelOptions' for matching models; per-request modelOptions from the caller still take precedence. Keys match the model id exactly, or use a '*' wildcard for a whole family (case-insensitive, e.g. 'qwen*'). Exact-id entries win over wildcard entries. Example: { "qwen*": { "temperature": 0.7, "top_p": 0.8 }, "deepseek-r1": { "temperature": 0.6 } }. Edit in settings.json.

github.copilot.llm-gateway.thinkingEffor.markdownDescription: Request-body key used for thinking effort, whether chosen in the chat model picker or with the **Set Thinking Effort** command. The default `reasoning_effort` (values `low` / `medium` / `high`) is understood by vLLM, LiteLLM, and most OpenAI-compatible servers; change it for backends that use a different name, e.g. `reasoning_budget` for llama.cpp.

enumDescriptions: Models the server reports as reasoning models (Ollama `thinking` capability, LiteLLM `supports_reasoning`), plus any model with a thinking effort already set in `perModelOptions`.
Every gateway model. Use this for servers that don't report reasoning support, such as vLLM or llama.cpp.
Never. The **Set Thinking Effort** command still works.
github.copilot.llm-gateway.thinkingEffor.markdownDescription: Which gateway models show VS Code's **Thinking Effort** control in the chat model picker. The choice is sent as `thinkingEffortParameter` on each request and overrides `perModelOptions` for that model; **Server Default** sends nothing.

github.copilot.llm-gateway.modelContextW.markdownDescription: Per-model context window override (total tokens), keyed by model id. Wins over what the server reports. Use when the server reports no context size — or the wrong one (e.g. llama-server router mode advertises nothing until a model is loaded). Keys match the model id exactly, or use a `*` wildcard (case-insensitive); exact-id entries win. Example: `{ "qwen2.5-coder-32b": 32768, "llama*": 123904 }`. Edit in settings.json.

github.copilot.llm-gateway.enableInlineC.markdownDescription: Experimental. Provide inline (ghost-text) code completions from your inference server, running **alongside** GitHub Copilot (not through it — VS Code does not expose bring-your-own-key models to its own inline suggestions). Requires a model/server that supports fill-in-the-middle via the `/v1/completions` `suffix` parameter (vLLM, llama.cpp, LM Studio, …). Leave disabled if you already use Copilot completions, to avoid two suggestions competing.

github.copilot.llm-gateway.inlineComplet.description: Model id to use for inline completions. Leave blank to use the first model reported by the server. Tip: point this at a small fill-in-the-middle / base model (e.g. a *-base or code FIM model) rather than a chat model for faster, cleaner completions.
Maximum tokens generated per inline completion. Lower values are faster and cheaper.
Milliseconds to wait after the last keystroke before requesting an inline completion. Higher values reduce load on the inference server while typing.
Per-request timeout (milliseconds) for inline completions. Kept short so a slow server doesn't block ghost-text suggestions.
Maximum characters of context before the cursor to send for inline completions. Lower values reduce latency but provide less context.
Maximum characters of context after the cursor to send for inline completions. Lower values reduce latency but provide less context.

github.copilot.llm-gateway.sessionAffini.markdownDescription: Name of an HTTP header that carries a per-conversation session id, sent on every chat-completions request so the gateway can pin the conversation to one backend deployment (avoids re-prefilling the prompt when load balancing moves sessions between runners). For LiteLLM set `x-litellm-session-id` and enable `session_affinity` in the proxy's `router_settings.optional_pre_call_checks`. The id is the conversation identifier supplied by Copilot Chat; when the installed build doesn't provide one, no header is sent and routing is unchanged. Leave empty to disable.

github.copilot.llm-gateway.showReplyToke.markdownDescription: Append a `Tokens: input … | output … | total …` line to the end of each reply, summing this gateway's server-reported usage across that reply's internal tool-call rounds (a completed reply, not the whole chat). Off by default so replies look like native Copilot output — the same numbers are available from the status bar menu and VS Code's context-window widget. Requires the installed Copilot Chat build to supply private, unstable per-request identity fields; if it doesn't, no line is added and nothing else changes.

github.copilot.llm-gateway.usageEndpoint.markdownDescription: Path of the gateway's daily token-usage endpoint, joined onto the Server URL. When it answers with `remaining_tokens` (plus `daily_limit`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `total_tokens`), the status bar shows the tokens left today and the hover / menu show the full breakdown. Servers without the endpoint answer 404 once and nothing is shown. Must be a path, not a full URL, so your API key is never sent to another host. Leave empty to turn the feature off.

github.copilot.llm-gateway.usageRefreshI.markdownDescription: Seconds between background refreshes of the daily usage (minimum 30). Usage is also refreshed shortly after every chat request and when the quota resets. Set to `0` to refresh only after requests and on demand.

github.copilot.llm-gateway.usageWarningP.markdownDescription: The status bar turns **yellow** when the remaining daily tokens are at or below this percentage of the daily limit.

github.copilot.llm-gateway.usageCritical.markdownDescription: The status bar turns **red** when the remaining daily tokens are at or below this percentage of the daily limit. `0` means red only once the limit is reached (it is always red then).

github.copilot.llm-gateway.loopGuardRepe.markdownDescription: Stop a response when the model gets stuck repeating the same text or thinking over and over, close the request so the server stops generating, and add a short note explaining why. An explicit request to repeat something many times will also be cut off — turn this off if you need that.

github.copilot.llm-gateway.loopGuardTool.markdownDescription: Catch agent tool-call loops: the model making the same tool call with the same arguments and getting the same result round after round, or cycling through a short sequence of such calls. First it is warned through the tool result (**Loop Guard Tool Nudge After**), then the repeated call is blocked while any other call still runs (**Loop Guard Tool Block After**). Turn this off to disable both.

When the model makes the same tool call with the same arguments and gets the same result this many times in a row — or cycles through a short sequence of such calls (A, B, A, B, …) for this many rounds — add a warning to the tool result telling it to use what it has or change approach. `0` turns this off; values below `2` also turn it off.

When the same tool call — or the same short cycle of tool calls — repeats for this many rounds with identical results, block those exact calls (same tool, same arguments): the model is told so in the tool result, a note is shown in the chat, and if it makes one of them again it is withheld. Any other tool call still goes through, so the agent can change approach and keep working; if the model only repeats blocked calls, the reply ends. `0` turns this off; values below `2` also turn it off.

github.copilot.llm-gateway.replayReasoni.markdownDescription: Send the model's earlier reasoning back to the server as `reasoning_content` on assistant messages. Copilot Chat only passes back thinking from the current reply's tool-call rounds, so this matters mostly in agent mode. **DeepSeek** thinking mode with tools requires it (requests fail with a 400 error without it); **llama.cpp** and **LM Studio** chat templates use it to keep reasoning across tool calls. vLLM, Ollama and SGLang ignore it, and OpenAI or Azure OpenAI may reject the request because of the extra field. Adds the reasoning text to every request's input tokens.

Per-model override of **Replay Reasoning**, keyed by model id. `true` replays reasoning for that model and `false` turns it off, whatever **Replay Reasoning** says; models with no entry follow **Replay Reasoning**. Useful on gateways such as LiteLLM that serve DeepSeek next to OpenAI models. Keys match the model id exactly, or use a `*` wildcard (case-insensitive); exact-id entries win. Example: `{ "deepseek*": true, "gpt-*": false }`. Edit in settings.json.
